# The Operator — full script

*Generated 2026-10-19 by `modules/bbttcc-onboarding/tools/export-operator-script.mjs` from the module source. Re-run it after any copy change; do not edit this file by hand.*

The Operator is the glitchy tutorial daemon that narrates onboarding. `*bzzt*`, `—static—` and em-dash stutters are performance notes: a glitch, a dropped frame, a cough in the signal. ⟨…⟩ marks a name the game fills in at run time (the steward, the Domain, the rig). Lines separated by `  /  ` are alternatives — the game picks one by situation; record each.

Every line has an id (e.g. `meatsuit.03`, `tour.raid-console.05`) so a recording can be keyed to it later.

---

## Part I — The induction (Alpha arc, in run order)

### Incarnation `incarnation`

**`incarnation.01`** Forge's still warm whenever you are. Rerun onboarding when you've picked a body.

**`incarnation.02`** The forge needs clay your permissions don't carry, One. Flagging the GM— *bzzt* —try again once they hand it over.

**`incarnation.03`** No meatsuit on file. Good — blank slates pour cleaner. Opening the forge: answer honestly, the Tree sorts the rest.

**`incarnation.04`** Forge closed, nothing poured. The offer stands — rerun onboarding whenever you're ready to be somebody.

**`incarnation.05`** Poured, cooled, and breathing: ⟨name⟩. That's you now — the sheet is the mirror. Continuing incarnation— *bzzt*

**`incarnation.06`** Connection established. You were The One — a perfect run, god-mode earned, a story told true enough to become load-bearing in the weave of things.

**`incarnation.07`** So we spun you back in to fix what broke. The catch— *bzzt* —you'll be doing it from inside a homemade Foundry video game. Mine. Try not to touch the walls.

**`incarnation.08`** You're in, ⟨steward name⟩. Wiggle the fingers, check the seams. Next module loading— *bzzt*

**`incarnation.09`** ⟨steward name⟩, under the ⟨Domain name⟩ banner. Rostered. Let's see what the two of you can break.

**`incarnation.10`** A body needs a banner, One. Before you drive, claim, or raid, the world wants to know: in whose name?

**`incarnation.11`** No banner, no problem — for now. Some beats ahead need one; I'll ask again when the world does.

**`incarnation.12`** ⟨Domain name⟩ — raised, rostered, and yours. Banks seeded, reputation unwritten. Best possible start— *bzzt* —nowhere to go but everywhere.

**`incarnation.13`** Parked out front: ⟨rig name⟩ — ⟨flavor⟩. Yours to drive, yours to answer for.

### Test the Meatsuit `meatsuit`

**`meatsuit.01`** Body's warm. Let's make sure it works before something tries to end it. Open your sheet — that's YOUR interface now, not a tutorial mock-up.

**`meatsuit.02`** Those are your ABILITIES — the entries with a play button, Principles tab and the rest. Click through them. See what each one does. Nothing out here counts: spend freely, swing at the straw fellow if the mood takes you. When you've seen enough, hit my button and we roll on.

**`meatsuit.03`** *bzzt* There it is — the meat answers the mind. Keep poking, One; out here it's all reversible.

**`meatsuit.04`** Reflexes intact, soul bolted in. SOMA BREAK — everything you just spent is restored; the sim picks up the tab. The straw adversary sends its regards— *bzzt* —dismissing it now.

### Test the Driving `driving`

**`driving.01`** Every Steward gets a rig. Yours is parked trackside — let's see if you can move it without folding it into a wall.

**`driving.02`** No rig on file— *bzzt* —minted you a Hexmobile on the house. Don't get attached.

**`driving.03`** Getting aboard: select your Steward's token, then RIGHT-CLICK it to open the token HUD and press the 🚚 truck button — that boards the nearest rig and seats you. Your Steward's token tucks into ⟨rig name⟩; from here you drive the rig, not the body.

**`driving.04`** The moment you're seated your selection jumps to ⟨rig name⟩ itself — that's deliberate. The lit-up token is the one you move now. Your Steward is inside it, riding along.

**`driving.05`** Seated? Now STEER — watch for the blue ring. (Steer spends a pilot action; if it balks, start or advance a combat turn to refresh one.)

**`driving.06`** Then the fun part: four dead vehicles squat on your track — real rigs, just nobody's driving them any more. Put every one back into scrap. Cleanest way is the guns: target a wreck and fire. RAM works too — target it, use Ram — but physics bills both parties, so you'll wear half of what you deal. Clear all four before that storm at the far end gets bored.

**`driving.07`** Couldn't find or mint a rig for your Domain. Make sure you lead a Domain, then re-run this beat. Skipping the test track for now.

**`driving.08`** Moving, wrecking, surviving — the whole grammar of the road. The rig'll forgive you; the terrain won't. Parking it — next module.

### Stewardship — Claim `stewardship_claim`

**`stewardship_claim.01`** Now the real work — stewardship. A hex is yours to shape, but first you have to CLAIM it. This one's a sandbox; nothing you do here touches the living world.

**`stewardship_claim.02`** See the hex below — unclaimed, neutral ground. Make it yours. Your steward's writ handles the filing; you just give the word.

**`stewardship_claim.03`** No Domain on file to claim under— *bzzt* —waving it through. Hold a Domain and the banner's real.

**`stewardship_claim.04`** Claimed. The hex knows your name now. Let's see what it costs to RUN it.

### Stewardship — OP & Turn `stewardship_turn`

**`stewardship_turn.01`** Your treasury — OPERATIONS POINTS. Economy ⟨fmt(b.economy)⟩, Violence ⟨fmt(b.violence)⟩, Diplomacy ⟨fmt(b.diplomacy)⟩. Every order spends from these buckets; they refill each Turn, capped by your tier.

**`stewardship_turn.02`** Operations Points — OP — fund every order you give. They refill each Turn, capped by your tier.

**`stewardship_turn.03`** Now the heartbeat that refills them: the TURN. Advancing one regens your OP toward its caps, resolves every queued order, and ticks the clock. We'll run a true PREVIEW — all rhythm, zero consequences.

**`stewardship_turn.04`** That's a Turn — previewed. In the living world it'd refill your OP and resolve every queued order. Nothing was committed here. You've got the rhythm.

**`stewardship_turn.05`** Stewardship: learned. You can hold ground and run it. One thing left before the real test— *bzzt* —you'll have to GO somewhere dangerous.

### Outfitting `outfitting`

**`outfitting.01`** Before you cross into hostile ground, two problems: you're broke and you're under-dressed. Fixing both— *bzzt*

**`outfitting.02`** A training stipend just topped up ⟨Domain name⟩ — up to what your tier can hold, not a mark more (Economy +⟨econMarks⟩ marks). Check that banner's sheet, not an older one.

**`outfitting.03`** ⟨Domain name⟩'s banks are already full to the tier cap — nothing to top up. Spend freely.

**`outfitting.04`** This is the LONG MARKET. I've already set the buyer to ⟨Domain name⟩ and the receiver to ⟨steward name⟩ — if either box reads "(Select)", pick them yourself or the till refuses you.

**`outfitting.05`** Buy what you can afford and can actually USE — your sheet warns you when a weapon or armor sits beyond your training. Watch the price line: it's in MARKS, and ten marks is one OP. And gear does nothing in a duffel bag: EQUIP it from your sheet once it arrives.

**`outfitting.06`** Look at you — dressed for the apocalypse you're about to drive into. The Syndicate won't know what pulled up.

### The People You Know `crew_occult`

**`crew_occult.01`** Before you point a weapon at anything — you're not alone out here, and the game knows it. *bzzt* Crews and associations are people you hire. The Muster in Allesh-Gilliam signs them, by the turn.

**`crew_occult.02`** Before you point a weapon at anything — you're not alone out here, and the game knows it. *bzzt* Two lines on your sheet decide what your whole faction can do.

**`crew_occult.03`** Sheet's up. Flip on EDIT mode (the pencil, top right) and find Awesome Crew and Occult Association in the identity block. Pick one of each — anything; you can change them later.

**`crew_occult.04`** That's your Echo Assets panel — every Crew and Association you carry, with ROSTER and INVOKE on each row. Open a roster, hit ✨ Suggest members, and mint one of them into a real person.

**`crew_occult.05`** Your Echo Assets panel lives on the sheet — that's where each Crew and Association gets its ROSTER and its once-a-scene INVOKE.

**`crew_occult.06`** Good. People are infrastructure, One — hired by the turn, and the only kind that argues back. One spotlight a scene; spend it on the moment that deserves it.

**`crew_occult.07`** No new maneuvers off that pairing yet — the grant shows up once the contract is signed at the Muster. Your GM can confirm it.

**`crew_occult.08`** ⟨Domain name⟩ can now attempt ⟨keys.length⟩ granted maneuver⟨keys.length === 1 ? "" : "s"⟩: ⟨named.join(", ")⟩⟨keys.length > 6 ? "…" : ""⟩. Look for the ✦ badges when the story opens a fight.

### Surge `surge`

**`surge.01`** Next: the currency nobody explains until it's too late. *bzzt* Surge.

**`surge.02`** Conflict tab, ✦ Surge panel — you're holding ⟨cur⟩. Open Spend and read what's on the menu. You don't have to buy anything; just learn where the shop is.  /  Conflict tab, ✦ Surge panel. You're empty right now — the bank fills the moment your dice start exploding. Open Spend anyway and read the menu so you know what you're saving for.

### Graduation `graduation`

**`graduation.01`** A body that works, a rig that moves, a hex with your banner on it, a Turn you've felt tick, gear on your back, people you know how to hire, Surge in the bank. That's a Steward on day one.

**`graduation.02`** Training's done, One. No more sandbox. Your first fight, your first deal and your first con will come to you on the road — the story opens the table, you decide whether to sit. From here it's the real Bad Eden — your hold, your rig, your Domain, live in the weave. Go fix what broke. *bzzt*

**`graduation.03`** Three consoles, four anchors, one circle, and something that tried to unmake the whole board and had to sit down at a table instead. Battle, heist, parley — you can take ground any way the moment demands. That's a Steward.

**`graduation.04`** Training's done, One. No more sandbox, no more straw adversaries. From here it's the real Bad Eden — your hold, your rig, your Domain, live in the weave. Go fix what broke. *bzzt*

**`graduation.05`** Connection handed off. You're live. Good luck, One — you'll need it. *bzzt* —Operator out.

### The Reality Dials `manifestations` — *Beta-only, cut from the Alpha induction*

**`manifestations.01`** Last classroom module, and it's the one the whole setting hangs on. *bzzt* Manifestations — how a Steward argues with reality and occasionally wins.

**`manifestations.02`** Theory's done. Now build one — the Manifestation Engine walks you through it step by step. Make something small and useful; you'll be firing it in a minute, and then again for real.

**`manifestations.03`** Engine won't open from here — *bzzt* — use the Manifestations tab on your sheet and hit the build button.

**`manifestations.05`** ⟨ctx._maniName⟩ is yours now — it goes where you go. Keep it in reach; you're about to need it.  /  You can author manifestations whenever the mood takes you. Keep at least one loaded before trouble finds you.

**`manifestations.06`** Surge in the bank, something of your own making in your hands, and people you can hire when the job needs them. That's a Steward. *bzzt* — Now we find out whether any of it survives contact.

### The Proving Ground `combat_sim` — *Beta-only, cut from the Alpha induction*

**`combat_sim.01`** Gear's bought, the Muster knows your name, and you're carrying something you built yourself. Now the part the manuals skip: what all of it does when something is trying to end you. Proving Ground, live-fire. *bzzt*

**`combat_sim.02`** Ground rules. Two kinds of thing come at you out here. QLIPHOTHIC are hollow — a shape with nothing living in it. Kill them; there's nothing to save. SENTIENT are people. People fold when they're losing, and a folded enemy is a saved one.

**`combat_sim.03`** You can kill the sentient ones. I won't stop you, and neither will the rules. It'll just show up on your DARKNESS track, and it stays there. That's not a punishment, One — it's a receipt.

**`combat_sim.04`** Simulation closed. ⟨t.husksDown⟩ hollow put down, ⟨rig name⟩ vehicle⟨rig name⟩ wrecked, ⟨t.saved⟩ spared, ⟨t.killed⟩ killed⟨talkedBit⟩.

**`combat_sim.05`** And some of them you TALKED past. No blood, no Darkness, nothing owed — the outcome most Stewards never even look for. Top marks, One. The Bad Eden will not always answer to words, but you'll know the ones that do.

**`combat_sim.06`** You saved some and you didn't save others. That's the honest answer most Stewards give, and Darkness sits at ⟨t.darkness > 0 ? `+${t.dar…⟩ because of it. Carry it and keep going.

**`combat_sim.07`** Clean, fast, and nobody walked away. It works. It always works. Ask yourself in ten turns whether it was still worth what it cost.

**`combat_sim.08`** Everyone who could be spared was spared. Harder than killing, every single time. Darkness track's clean — I noticed, and so will other things.

**`combat_sim.09`** Field's clear. Whatever else the Bad Eden takes from you, it won't be by surprise now.

### The Proving Ground — Trials `proving_trials` — *Beta-only, cut from the Alpha induction*

**`proving_trials.01`** Wiping the ledger. The floor grows its teeth back— *bzzt* —four sigils, four relics, same rules.

**`proving_trials.02`** — *bzzt* — hold. Hold. Something just reached into the world model from OUTSIDE and started pulling.

**`proving_trials.03`** Someone is trying to CRASH the game, One. Not your character — the game. And you are the only thing in here with hands and a tutorial's worth of privileges.

**`proving_trials.04`** Four sigils are holding the Proving Ground together. Whatever's chewing on us is prying them loose one at a time. Get to each one, take what's anchoring it, and bring all four to the great circle before the floor stops being a floor.

**`proving_trials.05`** Walk onto a sigil to take its relic. Move your token — this is the map, not a menu.

**`proving_trials.06`** ⟨n⟩ of ⟨PG_TRIALS.length⟩ anchors in hand. The pull's still there — I can feel it in the tick rate — but the ground will hold long enough for what comes next.

### The Final Show Down `final_showdown` — *Beta-only, cut from the Alpha induction*

**`final_showdown.01`** The great circle won't take you — ⟨held.length⟩ of ⟨PG_TRIALS.length⟩ anchors. It isn't being coy, One, it's being LOAD-BEARING. Go back for the rest.

**`final_showdown.02`** Four anchors, one circle. Step in and it closes behind you — that's the point of a circle.

**`final_showdown.03`** Whatever's been pulling at us is going to have to come through in person to finish the job. Good. In person, it can be HIT. *bzzt*

**`final_showdown.04`** You've fought all three ways by now — Battle, Heist, Parley. This is where you stop practising. How do you want to go in?

**`final_showdown.05`** A classmate's already at the door, picking how the class goes in. Hang on.

**`final_showdown.06`** The class is going in ⟨rig name⟩. You're with them.

**`final_showdown.07`** And there it is — the circle just closed behind you. Told you it would. Nothing gets out— *bzzt* —which cuts both ways.

**`final_showdown.08`** The small ones were never people. The big one is the hand on the lever.

**`final_showdown.09`** — the circle just OPENED. Not from your side. *bzzt* Hold. Hold—

**`final_showdown.10`** — wait. Something's coming in on a channel that shouldn't exist. It's not attacking. It's TALKING.

**`final_showdown.11`** The channel reaches out and FOLDS — *bzzt* — a room that wasn't in the world model a second ago. A court. Whatever's talking wants this done formally.

**`final_showdown.12`** It's a messenger. Unarmed, badly rendered, and carrying paperwork. *bzzt* — I did not have this on the list.

**`final_showdown.13`** It hands you ⟨granted.length === 2 ? "tw…⟩: ⟨granted.join(" and ")⟩. Those are RECEIPTS, One — real ones, in your Domain's hand, playable the moment the parley opens.

**`final_showdown.14`** It hands you its paperwork — though the court's filing system just refused it. Your GM can add the secrets by hand if it matters.

**`final_showdown.15`** So here's the shape of it. You can finish what's in the circle — it's losing, and nobody would blame you. Or you can take the surrender, open the parley, and find out what was so frightened of this place that it tried to unmake it.

**`final_showdown.16`** ⟨camePlain⟩. Either way it's talking now. Your GM runs the parley from the Raid Console — a PARLEY, not a Battle. I've pointed it at you.

**`final_showdown.17`** However that ended — it ended with words on the table. Remember that you had the option. Most things in Bad Eden won't offer it twice.

**`final_showdown.18`** Circle's quiet. The game is still here, and so are you. *bzzt* — I'd call that a pass.

**`final_showdown.19`** Training's over, One. Whatever tried that is still out there, and now it knows your name. Go be worth knowing.

**`travel.02`** Two holds ahead: your Forward Camp, and the Syndicate's. Plot a course and TRAVEL across — open your Travel interface and make the crossing.

**`travel.03`** You're across. They've seen you now — no walking this back. Time to choose HOW you take them.

**`travel.05`** Your GM's console just lit up on your banner — they run the rounds. Pick your maneuvers; your Domain brings what it owns, and the GM calls it.

## Part IV — Interface tours

Each tour opens a REAL window and walks its parts. The Operator speaks the intro and outro; the step cards are read by the player (or voiced, if you like).

### The Meatsuit Interface (Steward Sheet) `steward-sheet` — player

**`tour.steward-sheet.intro`** Pulling up your chassis diagnostics— *bzzt* —your sheet. This is the meatsuit's control surface. Touring it top to bottom; everything here is live, so feel free to poke.

**`tour.steward-sheet.01` · Who the meat says you are**  
Your identity block: Path, Ancestry, Heritage and Doctrine set what your body can learn; the Faction pill links to the people who claim you.  
Initiation is your level — Tier gates the strongest gear, manifestations and faction plays.

**`tour.steward-sheet.02` · Faculties — the six dials**  
The six Faculties are your raw capabilities. Every check in the game reads one of them.  
The ⚀ button rolls a bare Faculty test (2d10, tens explode, + the Faculty) — used for contests and anything without a trained Aptitude.

> *Operator:* Six dials. The factory settings were better, but these are yours.

**`tour.steward-sheet.03` · Integrity & Stress**  
Integrity is the meat's hit points — run out and the body stops cooperating.  
Stress is psychic load: manifestation strain, horror, overreach. It recovers with rest and scene breaks; maxing it out breaks something you'd rather keep.

**`tour.steward-sheet.04` · Guard · Evasion · Resolve**  
Your three defenses. Guard turns hits aside, Evasion keeps you from being hit at all, Resolve holds the mind together against fear, coercion and the uncanny.  
Each has its own ⚀ roll (2d10 explode + defense) when the world tests you directly. The chips underneath list immunities ⦿, resistances ◑ and vulnerabilities ▲.

**`tour.steward-sheet.05` · The tabs**  
Everything else lives behind these: Steward (this overview), Domain (your holdings, once you have one), Conflict (fights), Aptitudes (trained skills), Manifestations (your powers) and Inventory.  
More tabs open up as you grow. We'll hit the important ones now.

**`tour.steward-sheet.06` · Aptitudes — trained skill ranks**  
Aptitudes are Faculties with training. Ranks run 0–5 and each rank stacks a permanent benefit: Trained stops fumbles, Proficient rerolls your lowest die, Expert floors dice at 4, Master rolls 3d10 drop-lowest, Legendary auto-succeeds once per scene.  
Hover any rank label for the full accrued list.

**`tour.steward-sheet.07` · Manifestations — the reality dials**  
Your manifestations live here — cast from this tab, sustained against your Clarity.  
New ones come from your Path as you grow; the GM can grant a custom working.

**`tour.steward-sheet.08` · States — what's riding you**  
Active conditions, buffs, debuffs and lingering effects. Temporary ones list their clock and fall off when it runs out.  
If something feels wrong with your numbers, look here first — something usually is.

**`tour.steward-sheet.09` · Inventory**  
Carried gear, weapons and armor. Items you lack the training to use are flagged — untrained armor and weapons work badly, when they work at all.  
Equip state matters: only equipped items contribute.

**`tour.steward-sheet.10` · The Work**  
The long game — repairing the world, not just surviving it. Progress here tracks your part in the repair and unlocks the campaign's highest-tier play.  
It fills slowly. That's the point.

**`tour.steward-sheet.11` · Edit mode**  
The ✎ toggle exposes the raw inputs — direct rank edits, identity fields, the normally-locked plumbing.  
Day to day you leave it off; the sheet plays itself through clicks and rolls.

**`tour.steward-sheet.12` · Your Domain — the bigger body**  
You aren't just a body — you're a stake in a faction. The → button opens its sheet: OP banks, territory, politics, the strategic layer.  
That interface has its own tour when you're ready.

> *Operator:* Meatsuit: toured. Next size up is the faction — a body made of people. Different manual— *bzzt* —same principle.

**`tour.steward-sheet.outro`** Tour complete. The meatsuit manual is— —static— —is you, now. Hover anything on the sheet for the fine print.

### The Bridge (Steward ↔ Faction OP) `bridge` — player

**`tour.bridge.intro`** Opening the Bridge — the exchange rate between your meat and your movement. Everything you burn here, somebody collects on later. That's not a warning, it's— *bzzt* —it's accounting.

**`tour.bridge.outro`** Bridge tour complete. Sacrifice makes the faction strong; backing makes you dangerous; Blood Debt makes the world remember. Spend accordingly.

### The Bigger Body (Faction Sheet) `faction-sheet` — player

**`tour.faction-sheet.intro`** Opening your Domain — a body made of land, people and leverage. Same idea as the meatsuit, bigger stakes, slower heartbeat. One Turn per beat.

**`tour.faction-sheet.01` · Identity & vitals**  
The faction at a glance: crest, name, power-level status, and Total OPs against your budget.

**`tour.faction-sheet.02` · The OP Bank — nine kinds of power**  
Banked Operation Points across nine tracks — Violence, Nonlethal, Intrigue, Economy, Soft Power, Diplomacy, Logistics, Culture, Faith.  
The bank persists across Turns and pays for everything: raids, markets, backing, builds. Bank math: 1 OP = 10 marks. Hover any column header for what that track buys.

> *Operator:* Nine currencies. Your enemies only ever count one of them. That's how you beat them.

**`tour.faction-sheet.03` · The dashboard tiles**  
Big-number tiles with trend arrows — Loyalty, Darkness. These update automatically each Turn; the arrows tell you which way the wind is blowing before the numbers get dangerous.

**`tour.faction-sheet.04` · Faction health tracks**  
The internal weather: Loyalty (adherence — low risks defections), Darkness (Qliphothic taint — corrupts rolls and recruits).  
All update automatically each Turn. Hover each for the full mechanics.

**`tour.faction-sheet.05` · Organization Points — rolling power**  
Each track has a Value plus your Roster's contribution. The ⚀ rolls 2d10 (10s explode) + Value + Roster.  
Every 10 rolled banks Momentum. The +/− arrows adjust the bank by 1.

**`tour.faction-sheet.06` · Momentum — the strategic surge**  
Momentum banks +1 for every 10 rolled on OP checks and resets each Turn — spend it or lose it.  
The menu: 1 arms +1d10 on your next OP roll, 2 forces an opposed reroll, 3 refunds an OP cost, 5 is Reshape Strategy (GM-gated).

**`tour.faction-sheet.07` · Political Pressure**  
Your people have opinions. The Center is the dominant philosophy; Drift (−100..+100) is pressure against it, escalating the State: Stable → Strained → Fractured → Rupturing.  
Rupturing factions can split or flip. Soft-power campaigns, atrocities and succession crises all feed Drift.

**`tour.faction-sheet.08` · Activities — where fights arrive**  
The Activities tab is where the Domain acts. Battle, Heist and Parley come to you through the story — when one is offered, the Raid console opens here already aimed. Your Domain brings what it owns; the GM resolves the rounds.  
The Raid console has its own tour.

**`tour.faction-sheet.09` · The Next Turn queue**  
Strategic actions staged here fire when the GM advances the Turn (Apply). Anything flagged 'Cannot afford' will fizzle — check your bank before the Turn ticks.

**`tour.faction-sheet.10` · Quest Log**  
Your faction's open and completed quests — the story's ledger of what you've promised and delivered. Opens in its own window.

**`tour.faction-sheet.11` · Receipts**  
Receipts — the leverage a Parley makes for itself. A receipt is named for the table that made it, plays only there, and is spent when that Parley ends.  
The Play button lights up during that Parley: that's when a receipt becomes a weapon.

**`tour.faction-sheet.12` · Assets — Tier & capacity**  
Faction Tier gates what you can field — higher tier, bigger plays, cheaper Bridge sacrifices.  
The capacity strip shows asset load; the pressure chips (Overextension, Upkeep, Risk) warn when the empire is heavier than the foundation.

**`tour.faction-sheet.13` · Owned Hexes — the land itself**  
Every hex the faction holds, with per-Turn yields. Open any hex sheet from here.  
Land is where OP actually comes from — the Hex sheet has its own tour.

**`tour.faction-sheet.14` · Relationships — the Roster**  
The people who ARE the faction. Each member's aptitudes contribute to OP rolls per track (totals = Value + Roster).  
This is you, by the way — your Steward's row feeds every faction roll.

**`tour.faction-sheet.15` · Trade inbox & history**  
Offers from other factions land here — Accept, Decline or Counter. The history card below is the receipts.  
Bigger deals (Allied Sends, brokered exchanges) run through the Exchange dialogs.

**`tour.faction-sheet.16` · War Logs — the memory**  
Everything the faction has done or suffered — Turns, commits, raids, outcomes. When you're arguing about how the war started, the answer is in here.

> *Operator:* The war log never argues back. That's what makes it the most dangerous document you own.

**`tour.faction-sheet.outro`** Domain toured. Your steward acts in scenes; your Domain acts in Turns. Keep both alive and the world starts answering to you.

### Faction Sheet — GM Controls `faction-gm` — gm

**`tour.faction-gm.intro`** GM channel. Same faction sheet the players see, plus the levers they don't. Touring the override surface— *bzzt* —use it gently or don't get caught.

**`tour.faction-gm.01` · The Edit toggle**  
This header button flips GM Edit Mode (a world setting) and re-renders the sheet.  
OFF, the sheet is what players see. ON, the GM Manual Edit fieldset appears on Overview.

**`tour.faction-gm.02` · GM Manual Edit**  
Direct writes to the canonical flags: OP bank per track (in marks) and Loyalty/Darkness.  
Stage values, add an audit note, then Apply commits everything at once — and logs a gm_adjustment entry in the War Logs. Clear discards. Copy ID grabs the faction's actor id for macros.

**`tour.faction-gm.03` · Political override & drift nudges**  
Override the faction's political Center outright, or nudge Drift by ±5/±20 to push a faction toward (or back from) Strained, Fractured, Rupturing. Reset zeroes the drift.  
Use for story beats the simulation didn't earn on its own.

**`tour.faction-gm.04` · Granting doctrines**  
The Add buttons on Maneuvers, Strategic Activities and Receipts are GM-only — grant from the Doctrines catalog, or drag entries onto the dropzones.  
Remove links revoke. Players can open and read what they hold, not change it.

**`tour.faction-gm.05` · Advance Tier**  
Runs the tier-advancement check: the report lists anything blocking (capacity, stability) and advances the tier when eligible.  
Tier feeds raid gating, asset capacity and Bridge pricing — it's the biggest single dial on a faction.

**`tour.faction-gm.06` · Stockpile adjustments**  
GM-only manual edits to the material stockpile — players get deposit/withdraw, you get the thumb on the scale.

**`tour.faction-gm.outro`** GM controls toured. Everything you apply through the Manual Edit writes an audit line to the War Logs — the world keeps receipts, even on you.

### The Land Itself (Hex Sheet) `hex-sheet` — player

**`tour.hex-sheet.intro`** Opening a hex — one tile of the world, with its own economy, weather and grudges. This is what your faction is actually made of. Stewarding it well is— *bzzt* —is the whole job, honestly.

**`tour.hex-sheet.outro`** Hex toured. Land makes OP, OP makes power, power protects land. Break the loop anywhere and the other two follow it down.

### Moving the Meat (Travel Console) `travel-console` — player

**`tour.travel-console.intro`** Opening the Travel Console. The map is not the territory, but this thing charges you OP for both. Plot the route BEFORE you pay for it— *bzzt* —radiation doesn't refund.

**`tour.travel-console.01` · The route table**  
Plot a multi-leg route across the hex map, price it, then execute it as one commitment.  
Your faction auto-detects from whatever token you had selected.

**`tour.travel-console.02` · Lead faction — who pays**  
The lead faction's OP pool pays for the route. It follows your selected token live; players see only factions they own.

**`tour.travel-console.03` · Building the route**  
Pick on Map lets you click hexes on the canvas to append legs. Auto-Plan A→B runs a shortest-path between two picked hexes and fills the legs for you.  
The manual-entry drawer below does the same from dropdowns.

**`tour.travel-console.04` · The legs — where the cost lives**  
One row per leg: terrain sets the OP cost (ley-gates discount up to 40%), the hazard chip flags environmental danger, and the weather chip prices the sky.  
A shield badge means someone in your party can mitigate that leg's weather. Hover any chip for the details.

> *Operator:* Every leg is a small bill. The route is the invoice.

**`tour.travel-console.05` · The estimate**  
Legs, distance, and total estimated OP — checked live against your faction's bank so you know if you can afford it before you commit.

**`tour.travel-console.06` · Projected radiation**  
Travel through bad sky costs more than OP: each leg's weather adds Radiation Points (0.5 to 3 per leg), bucketed into an exposure tier for the whole route.  
Hot routes are sometimes worth it. Sometimes.

**`tour.travel-console.07` · Vanguard abilities**  
Travel-relevant abilities from your roster — guides, weather-wardens, scouts. These surface automatically once a faction is picked and can mitigate specific legs.

**`tour.travel-console.08` · Joining factions — traveling together**  
Allied factions can ride along as one stack. Each passenger pays its own OP (scaled per faction) — the cost preview appears once someone joins.  
Allies only; the picker stays locked until you have some.

**`tour.travel-console.09` · Dive & Ascend — the third axis**  
Dive drops the faction into the underwater scene linked to the current hex (needs a depth-rated submersible); Ascend goes up to the aerial or orbital layer (needs a flyer or spacecraft).  
The world has floors and ceilings.

**`tour.travel-console.10` · Execute Route — the commit**  
Runs the route leg by leg: debits every traveler, rolls encounters (you'll be prompted; the GM's run silently), fires the travel visuals, and moves the world.  
GMs get an overrides prompt first — cost multipliers, encounter DC tweaks.

> *Operator:* Execute is the only button here that spends real money. The rest is window shopping.

**`tour.travel-console.11` · The log**  
Execution results land here — what was paid, what was rolled, where you ended up. If a leg fails, this is where it says why.

**`tour.travel-console.outro`** Travel toured. Cheap routes are slow, fast routes glow in the dark, and the weather hates everyone equally. Plan accordingly.

### The Long Game (Activity Planner) `planner-hud` — player

**`tour.planner-hud.intro`** Opening the Activity Planner — everything your Domain can do that isn't hitting someone. Slower than a Battle, cheaper than a war, and it compounds.

**`tour.planner-hud.01` · The strategic catalog**  
Every strategic activity your Domain can run this Turn — outposts, trade plays, propaganda, construction. Battle, Heist and Parley come through the story; this is everything else.  
Flow: pick a target, pick an activity, Plan it.

**`tour.planner-hud.02` · Target hex**  
Most activities aim at a hex — pick from the dropdown or click one on the map. The list offers the hexes you hold and the unclaimed ground next to a hex you hold at level 2: a Domain grows from held ground. The GM can bypass that.  
Rig-repair activities swap this for a rig picker.

**`tour.planner-hud.03` · Category pills**  
Filter the catalog by the OP track each activity leans on — the same nine currencies as everywhere else. The search box narrows further by name.

**`tour.planner-hud.04` · The activity list — tier-gated**  
Each row shows its Tier requirement, OP costs, and package group. You can run anything at or under your faction's Tier; UNLOCKED badges mark activities you've learned above tier.  
Click a row to select it.

> *Operator:* The locked rows exist. You just can't see them yet. Motivation— *bzzt* —included free.

**`tour.planner-hud.05` · The ⓘ icons — full rules on hover**  
Every activity carries a tip icon with its complete rules text — effects, costs, requirements. Hover or click. When in doubt, the ⓘ is the law.

**`tour.planner-hud.06` · Show Locked (GM)**  
GM-only: reveals tier-locked activities with their LOCKED badges and bypasses target filtering — for planning what a faction grows INTO, not what it can do today.

**`tour.planner-hud.07` · The tally**  
Your faction's Tier and how much of the catalog it can reach — available, locked, total. Watch this grow as the faction advances.

**`tour.planner-hud.08` · Plan Activity — the commit**  
Validates the target and stakes the activity — it lands in your faction sheet's Next Turn queue and fires when the GM advances the Turn (Apply).  
One activity per click; the war log records it as planned.

**`tour.planner-hud.outro`** Planner toured. Fights win rounds; planned activities win Turns. The Domains that scare people do both — and a Domain grows from held ground.

### The Sharp End (Raid Console) `raid-console` — player

**`tour.raid-console.intro`** Opening the Raid Console. Three ways to take what's theirs: Battle, Heist, Parley. Battle and Heist are fought on the battlemap in combat rounds; a Parley is talked out at the table. The story opens the table — a fight comes to you as a choice, you never start one yourself. If there's no live fight I've staged you a practice target— *bzzt* —it won't mind.

**`tour.raid-console.01` · The identity strip**  
Who's fighting over what: the target, the key this fight leans on (gold pill — the strength your Domain brings is read from it), and portraits of the attacker plus any coalition supporters.

**`tour.raid-console.02` · GM setup row**  
GM-only: the attacker, the raid type — Battle, Heist or Parley, each with its own maneuver set — the difficulty band, and the target (Pick Target grabs a hex off the canvas). The story usually sets all of this; the GM can improvise.  
Add Round starts the exchange once attacker + target + type are set.

**`tour.raid-console.03` · Your bank**  
What your Domain owns. Nothing here is spent in a Battle or a Heist — strength is what the Domain already is: its ops, its people, its allies. The GM sees attacker and defender side by side.  
In a Parley you may sweeten the deal: marks handed to the other side, in the open.

**`tour.raid-console.04` · Coalition support**  
Allied Domains backing the fight. Supporters add their strength to the line and fire their OWN eligible maneuvers each round.  
The GM adds or removes supporters here.

> *Operator:* Friends make the number bigger. That's what friends are for.

**`tour.raid-console.05` · Rounds — the heartbeat**  
A fight is a series of rounds. Open one and you see the strength line for each side — what the Domain brings, nothing to push — and the stake: open ground is the prize, built ground takes a Siege. Pick your maneuvers; the GM resolves the round and the outcome lands in this table.

**`tour.raid-console.06` · Maneuvers — the knives**  
Per-side maneuver picker inside an open round: each maneuver has a fire-mode badge and an ⓘ icon with its complete rules. Usable only hides what your Domain can't field.  
Availability gates on Domain tier, your class and Beat grants.

**`tour.raid-console.07` · Commit (Roll) — resolving the round**  
GM-only: resolves the round. A Battle is fought on the battlemap first, then called here — won, stalemate or lost; open ground changes hands with the field. A Heist runs the alarm; a Parley runs the influence duel at the table. The outcome colors the round log.

**`tour.raid-console.08` · Reset & End Raid**  
GM-only: Reset clears the rounds but keeps the setup; End Raid tears down the whole fight — rounds, supporters, target — and propagates the clear to every player's console.

**`tour.raid-console.outro`** Raid console toured. Remember the shape: the story offers the fight, your Domain brings what it owns, you pick the maneuvers, the GM calls it. No marks change hands in a Battle or Heist; a Parley can sweeten the deal.

### The Rolling Body (Rig Sheet) `rig-sheet` — player

**`tour.rig-sheet.intro`** Opening your rig — a body with wheels, guns and a payroll. Same rules as every other body you own: feed it, crew it, don't let Integrity hit zero.

**`tour.rig-sheet.01` · Identity — mobility, state, owner**  
The pills that matter: Mobility (stationary / mobile / hybrid) decides if this thing travels at all; State runs the output throttle — Parked yields 100%, Deployed 50%, Destroyed 0.  
The owner pill binds it to a faction; the duplicate button opens the Rig Builder pre-filled.

**`tour.rig-sheet.02` · The four tiles**  
Integrity is the rig's health — zero means destroyed. Tier and bracket gate what it can mount; Crew shows seated versus capacity; Output is current throughput after the state throttle.  
Mobile rigs get Deploy / Recall buttons right on the Integrity tile.

**`tour.rig-sheet.03` · Crew — who runs the meat-wagon**  
The frame defines role capacity — pilot, gunner, engineer, general crew. Drag a Steward or NPC onto a slot to board them; occupied slots open the sheet or disembark.  
No pilot, no steering: moving a rig in combat is a crew action.

> *Operator:* A rig with no crew is just expensive terrain.

**`tour.rig-sheet.04` · Combat — the three DCs**  
Guard is the DC against melee and rams, Evasion against ranged, Resolve against EMP and demoralize effects — bracket base plus tier.  
Below, the defense table cycles resist/immune/vulnerable per damage type.

**`tour.rig-sheet.05` · Weapons & heat**  
Hardpoints are slot-capped by the frame (the pill goes red on overage). Drop rig-weapon items to mount them.  
Firing builds heat — every shot adds +1, and a maxed heat meter locks the guns until it bleeds off.

**`tour.rig-sheet.06` · Gear — the frame is the law**  
The frame sets base Integrity, all three slot caps (⚔ weapons, ⚙ systems, ⚡ outputs) and which mobility types are legal.  
Systems (sensors, shields, comms) and Output modules install below, each against its own cap.

**`tour.rig-sheet.07` · Output — why the faction keeps it**  
Output modules yield resources to the owning faction every Turn, scaled by the state throttle. A parked rig is a little factory; a deployed one is a half-speed factory with a gun.

**`tour.rig-sheet.08` · Travel — speed & range**  
Authored speed, range and hazard resistance, plus the derived table converting hexes to feet and squares (1 hex = 30 ft, grid-aware).  
Stationary rigs don't have this tab — they ARE the hex.

**`tour.rig-sheet.09` · GM Edit**  
GM-only (needs Edit Mode on): manual overrides for integrity, tier, bracket and per-role crew capacity — the thumb on the scale when the frame math doesn't fit the story.

**`tour.rig-sheet.outro`** Rig toured. Parked rigs produce, deployed rigs fight at half output, destroyed rigs produce paperwork. Choose wisely.

### The Long Market (Market) `market` — player

**`tour.market.intro`** Opening the Market. Everything has a price; whether it's YOUR price depends on your faction's Economic Horizon. Hover the chips— *bzzt* —the chips know.

**`tour.market.outro`** Market toured. Standard Issue is free, ambition costs double, and artifacts aren't for sale to anyone. That's not a bug, that's an economy.

### The Treasury `banks` — player

**`tour.banks.intro`** Opening the treasury. Rule one of Bad Eden banking: the land's Marks and your stored gear sit in one vault, because you and the land are one being. Rule two— *bzzt* —there is no interest rate. The apocalypse ate it.

**`tour.banks.01` · One treasury**  
Marks are the land's energy and the vault holds gear — weapons, armor, kit, bound manifestations. Both are yours, because you and your Domain are one being.

**`tour.banks.02` · Store to**  
Only a Domain that hosts a Coalition chooses where a stored item lands. Everyone else stores into the one vault.  
Salvage refines into Marks on the way in — that's the main way loot becomes money.

**`tour.banks.03` · Carried — what can go in**  
Your bankable inventory, with tier badges and ⚡ salvage markers. Store moves the item out of your hands and into the vault.

**`tour.banks.04` · Stored — getting it back**  
The vault's contents. Take puts an item back in your hands. Nothing decays in here; the vault is the one place the world can't touch.

**`tour.banks.05` · The faction treasury**  
The Marks: one chip per pool, shown against its cap (full chips light up). Read-only here — Marks move through the land's turn, the Exchange and the Market, not by hand.

> *Operator:* This is the war chest. Everyone can see it. That's a feature.

**`tour.banks.06` · Coalition hosting & withdrawals**  
Owners and GMs can flip this faction into a Coalition Treasury host — allied factions gain a deposit destination, and a shared coalition vault appears.  
The recipient picker routes withdrawn gear to one of your stewards.

**`tour.banks.07` · The faction vault**  
Shared gear storage. Withdrawing needs manage rights AND an owned steward to receive the item — the vault never dumps gear onto the floor.

**`tour.banks.outro`** Treasury toured. Marks for the land, a vault for the gear, salvage refined on the way in. Sleep with receipts.

### Facilities (The Short Version) `facilities` — gm

**`tour.facilities.intro`** Opening the Facility Console — briefly. This window mostly exists to tell you it retired. Facilities got promoted to full rig actors; the console is the forwarding address.

**`tour.facilities.outro`** That's the whole console. For the actual facility interface, run the Rig Sheet tour — a facility is just a rig that decided to stop moving.

### Shaping the Land (Hex Create & Edit) `hex-craft` — gm

**`tour.hex-craft.intro`** GM channel. Opening the hex workshop — where the world gets its tiles. I'll open a real hex's editor; nothing saves until you press Save, so wander freely.

**`tour.hex-craft.01` · Create Hex — button, click, done**  
The creation flow: click this, then click anywhere on the canvas — the hex Drawing is created there (snapped, unclaimed wilderness) and its editor opens automatically. Esc cancels placement.  
I won't press it — the next canvas click after it would plant a real hex.

> *Operator:* One click arms it, the second click is real estate. No takebacks— *bzzt* —well, one Delete key of takebacks.

**`tour.hex-craft.02` · The Hex Configuration editor**  
The full hex editor — also reachable by Shift-clicking (or double-clicking) any hex on the canvas as GM.  
Nothing here persists until Save; Cancel or closing the window discards everything. Poke freely.

**`tour.hex-craft.03` · Name, owner, status**  
Owner binds the hex to a faction — its yields flow there each Turn. Status runs claimed / unclaimed / contested; contested hexes are raid bait by design.

**`tour.hex-craft.04` · Type × Size — the economic engine**  
Terrain Type sets the resource base; settlement Size multiplies it; Sephirot alignment adds on top; the modifier checkboxes below adjust the total.  
That computed number becomes the per-Turn yield row you see on the Overview.

**`tour.hex-craft.05` · Modifiers**  
Twelve toggles — Well-Maintained, Fortified, Radiation Zone and friends — each multiplying or adjusting the auto-calculated resources. These are the fast levers for making a hex feel lived-in or ruined.

**`tour.hex-craft.06` · Leylines & gates**  
The hex's mystical plumbing: primary resonance, flow state, purity, memory charge — and ley-gates, which link two hexes and discount travel through them (up to 40%), gated by faction tier and a lock.

**`tour.hex-craft.07` · Resources & the override switch**  
The five yield numbers. Normally auto-calculated from Type × Size × Alignment + Modifiers; tick Manual Override in the Save Behavior box to save exactly what you type instead.  
Override is for story exceptions — the auto-calc keeps the economy consistent.

**`tour.hex-craft.08` · The GM Manual Edit panel — live wires**  
Travel-cost override, development stage and lock, alarm level, and the campaign beat that fires when a party enters this hex.  
⚠ Unlike the rest of the form, Apply and Clear here write IMMEDIATELY — they don't wait for Save. Look, don't lean.

> *Operator:* Everything else on this form asks permission. These two buttons ask forgiveness.

**`tour.hex-craft.09` · Save vs Cancel**  
Save commits the whole form to the hex Drawing in one update. Cancel (or the window ✕) walks away clean.  
For this tour: walk away clean.

**`tour.hex-craft.outro`** Hex craft toured. Type times Size times Alignment plus Modifiers equals the economy — and everything on this form is a dial on somebody's future.

### The Heartbeat (Turn Driver) `turn-driver` — gm

**`tour.turn-driver.intro`** GM channel. This one isn't a window — it's the world's heartbeat. One button, one confirmation, and every queued promise in the campaign comes due at once.

**`tour.turn-driver.01` · The Bad Eden bar**  
Every GM tool hangs off this bar — Dashboard, Create Hex, Overview, Market, Campaigns, Story, Raid, Plan, Travel, and the one we're here for: Turn Driver, at the end. Position of honor.

**`tour.turn-driver.02` · Advance Turn — the button**  
Clicking this opens an 'Advance Turn' confirmation (No is the default — a stray Enter won't end the world). Yes runs the full advance with apply: true.  
I'm not opening it; this tour is a map, not a detonation.

**`tour.turn-driver.03` · What actually fires on Apply**  
In order: queued post-effects promote → planned raids and strategic actions consume → territory tracks run (hex yields pay out, 2 Materials pips → 1 Build Unit) → scheduled OP bonuses mature → OP regen → logistics pressure → cleanup → world turn +1.  
Then the end-hook wave: radiation decays and spreads, facility turn effects apply, tier stability checks, pressure recomputes, and every faction's Momentum resets to zero.

**`tour.turn-driver.04` · The dry-run — rehearse the heartbeat**  
game.bbttcc.api.turn.advanceTurn({ apply: false }) runs the whole pipeline as a preview — every mutation is skipped, including (as of today) the Momentum reset and pressure writes that used to leak through.  
Use it before any Turn you're nervous about.

> *Operator:* Rehearsal is free. Opening night costs everyone their Momentum.

**`tour.turn-driver.05` · Reading the aftermath**  
After a real Turn: the Dashboard shows the new territory state, the Overview shows every faction's health at a glance, and each faction's War Logs got a turn entry.  
If something looks wrong, the logs say what fired and why.

**`tour.turn-driver.outro`** Turn Driver toured. Dry-run when unsure, Apply when ready, read the Dashboard after. The Turn forgives nothing but it announces everything.

### Mission Control (Campaign Dashboard) `dashboard` — gm

**`tour.dashboard.intro`** GM channel. The Dashboard — every hex in the world as one editable spreadsheet. Powerful the way a chainsaw is powerful: keep your fingers where you can see them, edits save instantly.

**`tour.dashboard.outro`** Dashboard toured. Filter, fix, focus — and remember every cell you touch saves on change. The chainsaw does not have an undo lever, but it does have War Logs.

### The State of the World (Campaign Overview) `overview` — gm

**`tour.overview.intro`** GM channel. The Overview — every faction's vital signs on one read-only page. Nothing here can break anything; this is the window you open BEFORE opening the windows that can.

**`tour.overview.outro`** Overview toured. World-Health up top, faction health down the rows, Great Work on the far edge. When those three agree with your plans, advance the Turn.

### The Spine of the Story (Campaign Engine) `campaign-engine` — gm

**`tour.campaign-engine.intro`** GM channel. Opening the Campaign Engine — beats, quests, travel tables and the flow map, all in one machine. It's big. That's why I'm here. Hover anything for the fine print; the fine print is new.

**`tour.campaign-engine.01` · One machine, five rooms**  
A campaign is a spine: an ordered list of beats (story events that fire), a quest registry bound to hexes, travel encounter tables, and a flow visualizer.  
The five tabs are the rooms; everything here is GM-only — players see the Beat Mirror instead.

**`tour.campaign-engine.02` · The campaign list**  
Your campaigns, with the Active chip marking which one drives the world — the Story Director tick, Reality-Tear draws and turn announcements all read the active campaign.  
Run First Beat does exactly what it says: fires the opener beat and nothing else.

**`tour.campaign-engine.03` · Bundles — campaigns as cargo**  
Export a campaign to a portable bundle, import one in, remap its IDs to this world's actors/scenes/hexes, and scan for unresolved keys.  
This is how a campaign travels between worlds without dragging its skeleton behind it.

**`tour.campaign-engine.04` · The selected campaign**  
Metadata, description, and the faction roster this campaign concerns — the Settings button edits them.  
Active Factions matter: several engines filter their attention to the campaign's cast.

**`tour.campaign-engine.05` · Travel tables**  
Terrain- and tier-keyed encounter tables (travel_<terrain>_t<tier>) that the Travel Console rolls when parties move. Fix Travel Tables repairs the id wiring.  
Preview Roll is a true dry-run: it shows which beat WOULD fire, with a clearly-labeled 'Run This Beat Now' escalation if you actually want it live.

> *Operator:* Preview means preview now. The world and the button have— *bzzt* —reconciled.

**`tour.campaign-engine.06` · Beats — the story's ammunition**  
Every beat in the campaign, in firing order. Filters by text, type, turn gate and quest; the chips show fired-state, quest binding and turn gating (turn gates are advisory — the GM gets a whisper, not a lock).  
Reorder with the arrows; Set Index jumps a beat to a slot; Compact Order squeezes the numbering back to 1..N.

**`tour.campaign-engine.07` · Per-beat actions**  
Run executes the beat NOW — journal, audio, scene, dialog, world effects, time points, in that order — and soft-locks it behind the fired-chip confirm. Edit opens the Beat Editor (its own tour).  
Delete now scans the campaign for references first and offers 'Delete + Clear Links' — no more silent dangling routes.

**`tour.campaign-engine.08` · Quests — story bound to land**  
The quest registry: status lifecycle (edit, complete, archive, reopen), and hex links — bind a quest to territory, and players discover it when the hex is fog-revealed or you toggle its hint. GMs see everything; the hint switches control what players see.  
Pan-to-hex jumps the canvas; the faction sheets' Quest Logs read from here.

**`tour.campaign-engine.09` · The Visualizer — where you PLAY it**  
Every other room in this machine BUILDS the campaign. This room plays it. One quest at a time, drawn top-down: root at the top, branches for every choice and outcome. ● HERE is the last fired beat, ⏭ NEXT is where the story goes, and the road you have already walked glows gold. Dashed → stubs are doors into other quests — click one to jump.  
Scroll to zoom at the cursor, drag anywhere to pan, click a beat to select it: Run or Edit.

> *Operator:* The other tabs are the workshop. This is the— *bzzt* —cockpit.

**`tour.campaign-engine.10` · Quest — and Follow**  
The chart FOLLOWS the story by default: whichever quest the last fired beat belongs to is the one on screen, so after every beat it is already showing the right chart. Pick a quest here to look elsewhere (Follow switches off); ⟲ Follow the story snaps it back.  
▶ marks the quest the story stands in, ✓ the ones completed.

**`tour.campaign-engine.11` · The truth strip**  
Where the world stands, in one line: current ACT and its name, world turn, days spent against the month's budget, and how much of this quest has fired.  
When anyone asks 'where are we in the campaign?', the answer is this strip.

**`tour.campaign-engine.12` · The rail — three blocks, nothing else**  
▶ NOW: the quest you are in, the beat you are standing on, and one unmissable card for what comes next — on a brand-new campaign that card is 🎬 BEGIN with a big ▶. ✓ RECENT: the last five beats fired. 🔒 LOCKED: the choices the table has made and the quests it has completed.  
Every row: click to fly the chart there, ⓘ for the full description, ▶ to fire. Drag the left edge to widen.

> *Operator:* It starts with one button. It ends with a— —static— —a story you can read back.

**`tour.campaign-engine.outro`** Campaign Engine toured. Campaigns hold beats, beats fire the world, quests bind beats to land, and the Flow map shows you the whole nervous system. The Beat Editor has its own tour — that's where the deep magic lives.

### Anatomy of a Beat (Beat Editor) `beat-editor` — gm

**`tour.beat-editor.intro`** GM channel. Opening a real beat from your active campaign — the atom of the story engine. Five tabs, a lot of wiring, and a tooltip on every wire. Edits survive tab-hopping now; Save is still the only real commit.

**`tour.beat-editor.01` · Five tabs, one atom**  
Core (identity), Injection (when it fires on its own), Scene (what it shows), Choices (how players branch it), Effects (what it does to the world).  
All five tabs preserve in-progress edits when you switch — Save commits them to the beat.

**`tour.beat-editor.02` · Identity — id, label, type**  
The id is load-bearing: choices, outcome routes and encounter tables reference beats by id. Rename with care and re-check routes after.  
Type changes the beat's anatomy — encounter and cinematic types grow extra sections.

**`tour.beat-editor.03` · Quest linkage**  
Binds this beat to a quest, step and role. The golden rule from the fire-order work: put quest COMPLETION on terminal beats — child routes resolve before parent effects, so mid-chain completion can strand the quest.

**`tour.beat-editor.04` · Audio — intro-on-open**  
The beat's soundscape. Intro audio fires when the dialog OPENS (the locked design call), curtain-call rules handle the tail. Playlist sounds use their playlist volume; the volume knob here only governs raw file playback.

**`tour.beat-editor.05` · Injection — firing on its own**  
Tag-matched injection lets travel and world systems pull this beat in dynamically. Once-per-hex, cooldown turns and repeatable control re-firing; once-per-firing semantics are engine-enforced.  
The Governance quartet is visibly disabled with a 'not wired' badge — the injector reads those from trigger context, so the controls tell the truth until they're connected.

**`tour.beat-editor.06` · Scene — what the players see**  
Scene link and activation, journal page reveal, and NPC actor placement — the beat can dress the stage before the dialog opens.  
Cinematic-type beats get their transition block here.

**`tour.beat-editor.07` · Choices — the branches**  
Each choice routes to a next beat, optionally gated by a stat check with a DC and a separate failure route.  
Below the choices, the new Outcomes section authors beat.outcomes — the success/failure fallback routes that outcome-trigger beats and unrouted check failures resolve through.

> *Operator:* Every choice is a door. As of today, every door has a visible hinge.

**`tour.beat-editor.08` · World Effects — the payload**  
What firing actually does: territory outcomes, radiation deltas, faction effects, spark links, gate unlocks, turn requests, quest effects, war-log entries — applied in the engine's fixed order (hover the header for it).  
These fields now survive tab switches and row-adds like everything else; Save commits.

**`tour.beat-editor.09` · The injected panels**  
Casualties, faction GM effects, world modifiers, unlocks — panels injected by their engines about 50ms after render.  
Relationship Effects is live now: rows save in the mutation engine's shape, Reciprocal mirrors the row both directions, and old-format rows migrate on load.

**`tour.beat-editor.10` · Save — the only real commit**  
Save harvests the whole form and writes the beat; Cancel discards everything including panel edits.  
Tab switches no longer eat edits, but Save is still the only thing that writes to the campaign — close without it and the session never happened.

**`tour.beat-editor.outro`** Beat toured. The rules in one breath: complete quests on terminal beats, treat the id field as load-bearing, and Save before you close. Everything else, hover for.
